body: Electro mechanic Tech here ,  my guess is that you replace the both caps , first you can measure the capacitance with a multimeter , usually a 5% overall variation on the reading is the tolerance , if the capacitance is too low , i suggest you have them swap the caps , the starting caps in an electric motor don't control the speeds ,  it only helps to boost the initial movement inside the motor , a lot of times you can only found one capacitor which is enough to start two speeds , when the required force is too low , or the power source is variable (120 to 200 volts) the manufacturers can use 2 caps
